content.text: Looking at this diff, it's a pure UI refactor extracting a shared skeleton component. Let me verify by reading the new file and checking callers to confirm no untrusted data reaches the new `count` prop.

Verified. All call sites pass either a literal `3` or use the default `6`. The `count` prop is never fed by request data, URL params, or any attacker-influenceable source. The component only renders static `<EventCardSkeleton />` placeholders — no rendering of untrusted values, no sinks (shell, SQL, HTML dangerouslySetInnerHTML, filesystem, network, template), no auth checks, no data flow.

This is a pure presentational refactor: extracting a repeated skeleton grid into a shared component and updating three call sites. There is no security-relevant surface change.
